newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND COACH KIDD DISMISSES TALK OF SACKING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND COACH KIDD DISMISSES TALK OF SACKING.

text.p: Ireland coach Murray Kidd on Monday dismissed rumours that he faced the sack in Tuesday's meeting with Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) officials.
"A few of the players have been in touch with me today and they feel that our preparation (for the Italian game) was excellent," Kidd said in an interview on Irish national radio.
"The players felt maybe they let themselves down on the day...none of the players I spoke to blamed me for what has happened over the last few weeks."
Kidd said he was already working towards Ireland's opening Five Nations championship game at home to France on January 18.

The IRFU on Monday summoned Kidd to a meeting which, they said in a statement, would cover matters relating to the performance and the future preparation of the international team, who lost 39-37 to lowly Italy at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.
Irish media said on Monday that New Zealander Kidd was expected to be dismissed this week, following the mauling by Italy.
Since the start of last year's international championship Ireland have lost six of seven matches under Kidd, including an embarrassing 40-25 defeat by Western Samoa.
Ireland team manager Pat Whelan said after the Lansdowne Road debacle on Saturday that Ireland's play was "devoid of any concerted or discernible pattern".
